question: Advisor headcount over the last eight quarters across the five.

claims.text: Edward Jones - The 10-Q for the period ended 2025-06-27 (published 2025-08-08) shows financial advisors at period end of 20,309, against 19,589 a year earlier (+4%).

Edward Jones - The 10-Q for the period ended 2025-09-26 (published 2025-11-07) shows financial advisors at period end of 20,429, against 19,885 a year earlier (+3%). The average was 20,368 against 19,749.
Edward Jones - The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) shows financial advisors at year end of 20,425 for 2025, 20,125 for 2024 and 19,232 for 2023. The average for 2025 was 20,331.

Raymond James - On the fiscal 4Q25 call (published 2025-10-22), the CEO said the firm ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year. The 2025 10-K says the count rose because new recruits and trainees moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements. Neither source gives the advisor count. The count excludes advisors in the RCS division.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's Nov 2025 investor day deck (published 2025-11-05) gives more than 15K Wealth Advisors for Global Wealth & Investment Management (Merrill and Private Bank), as a single undated figure.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's. It is also a single point, not a quarterly series.

adjacent.text: On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-14), Bank of America's CFO said adviser attrition is now at near historic lows. This is a GWIM-segment statement with no headcount number.
adjacent.differs_because: It is a qualitative statement about attrition, not a headcount series, and it comes from the GWIM segment rather than Merrill alone.

adjacent.text: The Schwab 10-Q for 2Q26 (published 2026-08-07) says higher compensation and benefits reflect growth in headcount, including financial consultants and wealth advisors.
adjacent.differs_because: It describes headcount growth qualitatively, with no advisor count, and it covers financial consultants and wealth advisors only as part of total company headcount growth.

adjacent.text: A Raymond James recruiting page (content as of 2026-05-17) cites 940 advisors across 160 financial institutions.
adjacent.differs_because: It covers only the Financial Institutions Division, not Raymond James's total advisor count, and it is an undated web page, not a quarterly series.

gaps.what: Edward Jones: the evidence has period-end advisor counts only for 2Q25, 3Q25 and year-end 2025, not all eight quarters.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones 10-Q and 10-K financial advisor tables for each quarter, plus earnings releases

gaps.what: Raymond James: no quarterly advisor counts are in the evidence, only a 2% year-over-year rise at fiscal year-end 2025.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James quarterly earnings releases and financial supplements (Private Client Group financial advisor counts)

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley: wealth management advisor headcount is not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley quarterly Wealth Management financial supplements (financial advisor counts)

gaps.what: Schwab: financial consultant and wealth advisor counts by quarter are not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab quarterly earnings releases and supplements, investor day materials

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America quarterly GWIM supplements and earnings call remarks on Merrill advisor numbers
